Cold Open: test build
=====================

This is an unsigned build made by CI, for testing. It is not a release.
Your scripts are plain Fountain or .fdx files, so nothing you write here
is locked in.

In this folder:
- the app: "Cold Open.exe" (Windows), "Cold Open.app" (macOS) or
  coldopen-app (Linux);
- coldopen: the command-line tool, which also runs the MCP server for
  AI agents (coldopen mcp);
- licenses: Cold Open (GPL-3.0-or-later) and its two fonts (SIL OFL 1.1).


Starting it
-----------

Windows: double-click "Cold Open.exe". Windows SmartScreen may say
"Windows protected your PC", because the build is not signed. Click
"More info", then "Run anyway".

macOS: right-click "Cold Open.app", choose Open, then Open again. If
macOS says the app is damaged or can't be checked, run this in Terminal
and try again:
    xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine "/path/to/Cold Open.app"

Linux: run ./coldopen-app. It needs X11 or Wayland, and libxkbcommon.


What to try
-----------

1. Write a scene. A new script starts on a scene heading. Enter and Tab
   move between elements; the bar at the top says what Enter and Tab will
   give next. Ctrl+K (Cmd+K on macOS) opens the palette, which lists every
   command and its shortcut.
2. Save with Ctrl+S (Cmd+S). The first save asks where.
3. Try to lose work. While typing, end the app hard: Task Manager >
   End task on Windows, Force Quit on macOS, or kill -9 on Linux. Start it
   again. If the script was saved, open it: a dialog says what was
   recovered. If it was never saved, the app offers it at start-up.
   Nothing that was on screen should be missing.
4. Let an AI agent edit the open script. With Claude Code:
       claude mcp add coldopen -- "/full/path/to/coldopen" mcp
   Then ask it to open the script you have open in the app and make a
   change. You see the edit appear, a violet bar marks the changed block,
   and Ctrl+Z (Cmd+Z) undoes it. The status bar shows the agent while it
   is connected, with Disconnect and a switch to turn agent access off.
5. Export a PDF: Ctrl+Shift+E (Cmd+Shift+E).
6. Open an .fdx file, edit it, save it with Ctrl+S and open it again:
   it stays an .fdx file and nothing in it should be lost, including
   what Cold Open doesn't show. Save as converts between Fountain and
   .fdx by the extension you choose, and asks first about anything the
   other format can't hold. "Save a copy as .fdx" and "Save a copy as
   Fountain" are in the palette. A damaged .fdx file opens with a report
   of what was repaired; "Repair an .fdx file" in the palette writes a
   repaired copy and never changes the original.
7. Recovered versions (palette, start screen, or the button in the
   message after "Don't save"): changes Cold Open set aside instead of
   deleting, with a preview. Restore opens one as a new script.


Settings and files
------------------

settings.json, keymap.json (your own shortcuts) and flow.json (your own
element flow) live in:
- Windows: %APPDATA%\Cold Open
- macOS: ~/Library/Application Support/Cold Open
- Linux: ~/.config/coldopen

Scripts you haven't saved yet live in an "Unsaved" folder next to them
(%LOCALAPPDATA%\Cold Open\Unsaved on Windows), with a crash journal.

Drawing: Cold Open draws with the CPU on Windows and Linux and with the
GPU on macOS. On a 4K screen the GPU is smoother; the CPU uses far less
memory. Switch in the palette ("Draw with the GPU" or "Draw with the
CPU"); it takes effect at the next start.


Reporting a problem
-------------------

Say which system you used, what you did, and what you expected. If work
went missing, look in Recovered versions first. Keep the "Unsaved" folder
and any ".coldopen-journal" files next to your script (hidden on
Windows): they hold what was typed.
